subtitle: Transforming agricultural decision-making through integrated data and AI-powered insights.
mission: The shared infrastructure that turns Africa's fragmented agricultural data into decisions institutions can trust.
aim: Building Africa's agricultural intelligence layer — defragmenting and federating agricultural intelligence across Africa so decision-makers get usable intelligence, not just more data.

current_state.summary: Africa is the fastest-growing continent with more than 1.4 billion people and the youngest population in the world. Agriculture is the largest employer but remains one of the least efficient sectors due to poor data infrastructure.

core_problem.headline: Agricultural data exists but decision-makers lack clear intelligence.
core_problem.summary: Data exists across governments, institutions, research bodies, and private organizations — but it is fragmented, inconsistent, and difficult to access when decisions need to be made.

challenge.headline: Africa doesn't have a data problem. It has an intelligence problem.
challenge.summary: Agriculture is the backbone of the continent, yet the decisions that shape it are made without a clear view of the system. The data exists. It just can't be used when it's needed.

opportunity.headline: Agriculture is becoming one of the most data-intensive sectors in the global economy.
opportunity.summary: Driven by food security, climate resilience, and supply chain stability — yet most decision-makers still struggle to translate fragmented information into actionable intelligence. OpenTrace combines harmonised datasets with AI-powered interfaces to transform agricultural data into decision intelligence.

why_it_persists.headline: An impact failure, not a data failure.
why_it_persists.summary: The system cannot see itself clearly; well-intentioned investments underperform. Data is fragmented across authority levels, inconsistent across countries, siloed by sector, and rarely designed to be used together.

systemic_costs.name: Reactive policy
systemic_costs.description: Governments design reactive policies without a real-time view of production or risk.

systemic_costs.name: Late climate response
systemic_costs.description: Climate responses are ineffective; interventions miss regions and seasons that need them most.

systemic_costs.name: Agriculture priced as high-risk
systemic_costs.description: Banks, insurers, and investors treat agriculture as high risk; insurance penetration remains low.

systemic_costs.name: A generation excluded
systemic_costs.description: Data is abstract and technical, closed to the young people meant to inherit the sector.

without_reliable_intelligence: Financial institutions treat agriculture as high risk
The entire system operates below potential

agricultural_data_gap.headline: Information overload but insight scarcity.
agricultural_data_gap.summary: Africa lacks a unified platform that integrates agricultural datasets across institutions, countries, and systems.

what_we_are.headline: We are an infrastructure company.
what_we_are.summary: Ask ADZA is what you see. OFIA and ACF are why it works. We build infrastructure, not reports — infrastructure that persists beyond projects, improves with use, and creates shared understanding across institutions.

what_opentrace_connects.summary: All integrated into one structured intelligence platform.

ask_adza.name: Ask ADZA
ask_adza.description: OpenTrace's machine-learning-powered natural language interface. Users ask questions in plain language across web, mobile, and WhatsApp; institutions connect via API. No dashboards, no SQL, no analyst in the middle — validated, structured answers backed by reliable integrated agricultural intelligence.

acf.name: ACF
acf.description: Attaches confidence signals to analytical outputs based on triangulation across three tiers of evidence. Rather than uniform AI certainty, users see where evidence is strong, partial, or uncertain. Confidence levels increase as global, national/regional, and local field validation align.
acf.tagline: OFIA makes intelligence possible. ACF makes it honest.

ofia.name: OFIA
ofia.description: Core infrastructure that structures, harmonises, and version-controls agricultural datasets across global, national, and sub-national levels, making heterogeneous data usable together as decision intelligence.
does: Federates data across global, national, and sub-national levels
Enables comparability across time and geography
Powers consistent querying through Ask ADZA
Separates source data from derived intelligence
does_not: Does not own or enclose datasets
Does not function as a data marketplace
ofia.ip_note: The IP sits in the architecture, integration logic, and intelligence layer, not in the underlying data.

data_reconstruction.name: Data reconstruction
data_reconstruction.summary: Mimicking natural systems to close agricultural data gaps by reconstructing patterns across multiple sources when ground-level data is sparse.
does: Integrate fragmented climate, production, market, and research systems into a structured analytical layer
Triangulate signals across data layers instead of relying on a single dataset
Close critical gaps by combining global, national, and community-level sources
Reveal system-level patterns: production shifts, climate exposure, market dynamics
examples: Crop production trends using climate, yield, and market datasets
Climate stress patterns linked to declining yields
Production changes connected with food price movements
Emerging agricultural risks across districts and value chains

system_intelligence.name: System-level intelligence
system_intelligence.summary: Connects agriculture with broader systems for holistic understanding.

acf_tiers.label: Global & continental
acf_tiers.examples: Cross-country datasets, satellite systems, continental research, global agricultural institutions

acf_tiers.label: Regional & national
acf_tiers.examples: Government databases, ministries, national statistics, regional networks

acf_tiers.label: Ground & community
acf_tiers.examples: Local validation networks, cooperatives, NGO field reports, community data

federation.summary: OpenTrace defragments and federates agricultural intelligence by connecting data vertically across levels and horizontally across sectors — harmonised, versioned, and queryable.

principles: OpenTrace does not generate speculative answers
Transparency and reliability are core principles
All insights come from verified integrated datasets within the OpenTrace system
Every insight can carry a measurable confidence level via ACF

data_sources.summary: OpenTrace aggregates and harmonises data from multiple sources into a standardised framework.

platform_architecture.summary: Cloud-based intelligence infrastructure enabling real-time analysis at continental scale.

trust_and_sovereignty.headline: Your data stays yours.
trust_and_sovereignty.summary: OpenTrace respects African data ownership and governance. Partners retain control of their datasets while OpenTrace provides infrastructure to integrate and interpret them responsibly.
commitments: Source data stays under its original licence
Data stays where it lives — we federate, not enclose
Derived intelligence is kept separate from source data
never_do: Sell or monetise raw data access
Build black-box scores you can't interrogate

how_we_work.headline: A system you plug into, not a one-off project.
how_we_work.summary: Our role is narrow and disciplined: receive data where shared, integrate into OFIA, generate intelligence through Ask ADZA. Infrastructure, not consultancy.

steps.name: Receive
steps.description: Data shared on your terms; where, when, and if you choose.

steps.name: Integrate
steps.description: Harmonised and version-controlled inside OFIA, never enclosed.

steps.name: Generate
steps.description: Intelligence on top, every output scored by ACF confidence.

how_we_work.pricing_model: Free to contribute. Pay to leverage. Individuals use Ask ADZA; institutions connect via API.

business_model.summary: OpenTrace monetizes intelligence, not raw data.

audiences.value: Sharper, evidence-based policy and food-security planning.
Target programmes and monitor field conditions continuously.
Assess production, market, and regional risk with confidence.
Local insight in plain language, no spreadsheets required.
An accessible entry point into Africa's agricultural data.

government.headline: Decision intelligence for evidence-based policy
points: Monitor agricultural production, climate exposure, and market conditions across regions
Identify districts vulnerable to climate variability and food security pressures
Design better agricultural and food security policies combining climate, production, and market intelligence
Target investments (irrigation, extension, climate adaptation) more effectively
Explore patterns via Ask ADZA without manually reconciling fragmented data

development_partners.headline: From static reporting to continuous evidence-informed programming
points: Identify regions where climate, production, and food security risks overlap
Monitor how conditions evolve in programme regions
Target interventions toward greatest vulnerability in productivity, resilience, or food security
Communicate priorities and impact with stronger evidence via Ask ADZA

private_sector.headline: Risk awareness and market intelligence for agribusiness and finance
points: Understand climate variability, production volatility, and supply disruptions by region
Analyze production trends, yield stability, and regional supply for sourcing and supply chain planning
Assess agricultural exposure for banks, insurers, and lenders
Evaluate where production is expanding, stabilizing, or facing structural risk

farmers_communities.headline: Local agricultural visibility in plain language
points: Understand how production, rainfall, and growing conditions evolve locally
Track drought patterns and seasonal variability over time
See how market prices change across regions and seasons
Help cooperatives coordinate planting, aggregation, and market engagement
Examples: cooperatives tracking regional prices; farmer groups comparing rainfall; extension networks with localized insights

entrepreneurs.headline: Ecosystem intelligence for agri-entrepreneurs
points: See where crop production is expanding, stabilizing, or declining
Identify how climate variability affects productivity and supply
Understand demand, supply, and value chain evolution
Design innovations in logistics, inputs, finance, storage, and climate tech
Examples: storage startups spotting post-harvest challenge regions; logistics mapping production hubs; climate-tech analyzing regional risks

traction.partnerships: Research: IITA, CGIAR (formalising). Government: multiple conversations advancing. In conversation: multiple foundations, AGRA.
traction.feedback: Testing in-house with agricultural specialists ahead of V1.0; strong early feedback on usability, traceability, and decision relevance.

partnership_ecosystem.summary: OpenTrace operates through strategic partnerships for data quality, coverage, and credibility.
partner_types: Academic research bodies — agricultural research and innovation
Private sector contributors — data accessibility and utility
Community networks — ground-level data and actionable insights

growth.strategy: Deliberate, country by country. Deepen coverage and trust market by market before widening.

phases.name: Credibility
phases.description: Anchor in priority markets and validate with research partners like IITA and CGIAR.

phases.name: Depth
phases.description: Deepen data per country and formalise government partnerships.

why_partner.title: Systems change, not point solutions
why_partner.description: We build the shared layer everyone plugs into, not another standalone tool.

why_partner.title: Durable beyond any grant cycle
why_partner.description: The platform persists across projects and improves with every use.

why_partner.title: Aligned with open-data mandates
why_partner.description: We respect existing licences and funder requirements by design.

why_partner.title: African-led, for African realities
why_partner.description: Built for the continent's data, languages, and institutions.

vision.headline: Africa's agricultural future depends on intelligence, not just productivity.
vision.summary: OpenTrace aims to become the trusted intelligence backbone for agriculture across the continent — transparent, scalable, and designed for Africa's future.
